question.text: Let the sum of the maximum and the minimum values of the function $f(x)=\frac{2 x^2-3 x+8}{2 x^2+3 x+8}$ be $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}$, where $\operatorname{gcd}(\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})=1$. Then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to :

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{2 x^2-3 x+8}{2 x^2+3 x+8} \\ & x^2(2 y-2)+x(3 y+3)+8 y-8=0 \\ & \text { use } D \geq 0 \\ & (3 y+3)^2-4(2 y-2)(8 y-8) \geq 0 \\ & (11 y-5)(5 y-11) \leq 0 \\ & \Rightarrow y \in\left[\frac{5}{11}, \frac{11}{5}\right] \\ & y=1 \text { is also included }\end{aligned}$
